claim:adhesion-calibration.proposition: REVISED per the 2026-10-27 review: this is NOT a calibration of CPM contact energy J to vertex line tension, and the sheets are NOT established as physically matched. The CPM (23.6 um^2) and vertex (34.9 um^2) mean areas differ by ~48%, and the vertex shape statistics are nearly INSENSITIVE to tension_scale over 0.5..8 -- so tension is weakly/non-identifiable from this test. What this study honestly shows: the neutral adhesion strength lowers DIRECTLY to J and MONOTONICALLY (same sign) to line tension, a DIRECTIONAL relation only. A proper physical-observable calibration (relaxation time, interfacial length, deformation under force, migration mobility, neighbour exchange) with identifiability analysis is deferred to Stage 3 / BP-07.
evidence_refs: Neutral sheet playback — CPM vs vertex

claim:initial-state-fidelity.proposition: Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state -- every cell's centroid, size and type -- when the one backend-neutral blueprint is compiled onto each. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0); the vertex side is within a sub-cell residual (RMS ~1.2 um) and achieves a clean 1:1 identity for every cell (fraction_clean 1.0).

claim:flu-lung-crossparadigm.proposition: The ONE backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint compiles to BOTH the CPM (viva-cpm) and vertex (vivarium-tyssue) substrates and runs the Sego model WITH NAMED DEVIATIONS (V/L/C/F producers absent, latent-pool recruitment approximation) end-to-end on each. Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / recruitment mechanism is shared byte-for-byte across the two compiles, we test for a substrate effect against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread). On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference sits inside the same-backend seed spread, so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT the null (no detectable substrate effect -- NOT proof of equality). The one exception is raw infected-patch occupancy IoU, which trends ~25-35% below both same-backend baselines -- a candidate weak substrate signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds.
evidence_refs: Dynamics overlay — CPM vs vertex (I-count band)

claim:dose-response-crossparadigm.proposition: Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

pass_if.note: final(0.15) > final(0.03) for cpm/vertex x seeds {0,1}

evidence_refs: Dose response — initial load → final infection

claim:crossparadigm-equivalence.proposition: SCOPED to Claim 3 (scientific equivalence) — NOT blueprint fidelity, NOT biological validity. On cell FATE the two substrates are equivalent under a DEPENDENCE-AWARE reanalysis: the 6x6 grid's 36 cross + 30 same pairs reuse only 6+6 runs and are statistically dependent, so the unit of resampling is the RUN. A run-cluster percentile bootstrap gives Delta(same-cross) -0.0015, 90% CI [-0.003, +0.001], inside a +/-0.05 margin -- so fate agreement is equivalent. CAVEATS (reviewer): the +/-0.05 margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the tight CI reflects LOW between-run variance at this reduced scale, not strong power. The earlier pair-level TOST (p=5.6e-36) treated dependent pairs as independent and OVERSTATED significance -- retired as the headline. Exact spatial position is NOT equivalent (cross 0.08 vs same 1.00; ~8.5 um median drift; 1.0 at t0) -- a CANDIDATE representation effect (lattice COM vs relaxing polygon centroid), NOT yet causally isolated (BP-02/BP-04 will isolate it).

claim:substrate-divergence-counterfactua.proposition: In a MECHANICS-DOMINATED regime (strong differential adhesion + a strong chemoattractant gradient, no shared rules/ODE), the two substrates DIVERGE: the spatial equivalence test REJECTS equivalence (cross-backend spatial agreement 0.20 vs same-backend 1.00; TOST diff +0.80, margin +/-0.10). The divergence is mechanistically attributable -- the vertex fork's ActiveMigration climbs the gradient (type-A mean y 7 -> 17.9) while CPM's Metropolis chemotaxis barely moves it (y -> 10.7). This is the POSITIVE CONTROL for crossparadigm-equivalence: it proves the equivalence test can detect a real substrate difference, so the equivalence verdict on the Sego model is informative, not an artifact of an insensitive metric.

pass_if.note: cross spatial agreement << same; diff > margin
vertex final y > cpm final y

narrative.question: Can ONE backend-neutral blueprint express the whole Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) and run it faithfully on two different mechanical substrates — a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm) and a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue) — and where do the two substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live?

decisions.title: STAGE 1 (BP-01): formalize a versioned blueprint schema + canonical IR, separate from backend geometric init (units, coord frame, boundaries, tessellation-independent IDs, footprints, fields, contacts, latent states, seeds, init order, mechanism bindings, provenance, allowable loss).

STAGE 2 (BP-02/BP-04, extend initial-state-fidelity): prove blueprint fidelity beyond centroids/IDs — area, footprint, contact, adjacency, boundary, topology, round-trip, with explicit error measures and loss reports.

STAGE 3 (BP-07, supersede adhesion-calibration): the adhesion J<->tension mapping is NOT a calibration (~48% area gap, tension-insensitive CV). Calibrate to common physical observables; separate geometry/init/mechanics/numerical differences; identifiability analysis.

STAGE 4 (BP-05): V/L/C/F inputs have no producer and immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation — build a producer/consumer ledger, implement or clearly designate deviations, and ablate frozen inputs.

STAGE 4 (BP-06): the ±0.05 fate-equivalence margin is NOT yet biologically justified; the dependence-aware reanalysis is done (cluster bootstrap) but power under biologically meaningful perturbations is not established.

STAGE 4 (BP-08): biological fidelity to Sego 2022 is NOT validated — digitize figure/table/parameter anchors and compare predictive intervals on held-out data; no biology inferred from cross-backend agreement.
STAGE 4 (dose-response redefine): separate virion inoculum from seeded infected fraction; 6-10 graded doses x replicate seeds; it is currently directional-only, NOT a dose-response curve.
STAGE 5 (BP-09): compile a SECOND independent tissue blueprint through the same schema with no influenza-specific adaptations — the decisive generality test.
